editorial:
Imagine looking back at your best friends from elementary school and realizing you have all grown apart. That is exactly what you get with this story. You follow Patrick, Shiv, Rian, Oli, and Conor, five buddies who spent their youth skipping class and making wild plans for the future. Now that they are thirty, those big dreams feel like they are disappearing. The vibe is very grounded and honest, making you feel like you are sitting in the room with them as they deal with the boring and sad parts of becoming an adult. It captures that weird feeling of being stuck while the rest of the world keeps moving forward.

The acting is the best part here because the chemistry between the five leads feels totally real. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the emotional payoff at the end makes it worth the wait. If you love stories about friendship and growing up, you need to see this.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the group meets up one last time at their old childhood hangout. They finally admit that they failed to reach their big goals, but they realize that is okay. The twist is that Patrick has been hiding a job offer in another city. Instead of leaving in secret, he tells the group, and they all promise to stay in touch regardless of where life takes them.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about old friends and life struggles.
